correctness.rationale: The published Schur-cover relation specializes in \(A=C_{p^a}\times C_{p^a}\) to the determinant commutator \([\widetilde x,\widetilde y]=z^{x_1y_2-x_2y_1}\) with \(o(z)=p^a\). A clique spans an isotropic submodule. Smith normal form writes that submodule as \(U(p^iRe_1\oplus p^jRe_2)\); isotropy forces \(i+j\ge a\), hence order at most \(p^a\). Conversely every order-\(p^a\) subgroup has \(i+j=a\) and is isotropic. The stabilizer-index calculation gives the type counts, and their sum is the stated geometric series. The packaged exhaustive replay independently recovers the maximum cliques and type distributions in five small cases.

The 2025 comprehensive preprint gives the necessary abelian-p-group commutator formula and two low-exponent examples, but its full text does not state a clique-number theorem or classify and count maximum cliques for the homocyclic rank-two family. value.rationale: The foundational paper explicitly motivates graph-theoretic study of the deep commuting graph, and later work has expanded that program. The result gives a natural exact extremal invariant on the first non-elementary homocyclic family, not a small finite census: it determines the clique number for every prime and exponent, classifies every extremizer algebraically, and counts extremizers by isomorphism type. The theorem also clarifies how the \(p+1\) projective-line picture at exponent \(p\) changes at higher exponent, where noncyclic maximum cliques appear.
